source.title: Origins and mitigation of double descent in reduced order modeling
source.authors: A. Klishin; J. Kutz; Krithika Manohar

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text, including references, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests double-descent-like risk curves in sparse sensing and reduced-order models, a new setting distinct from the original supervised-learning settings.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own sparse-sensing and DEIM error results. Cited findings from other work and design choices used to define the experiments are not results. The paper does not sweep training epochs or training-set size.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in sparse sensing and reduced-order modeling: measurement noise and residual-mode contamination produce reconstruction-error spikes, and regularization suppresses them. Sensor count varies at fixed reconstruction rank; this does not directly test V4's increase in model capacity beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for static reconstruction: noise or residual-mode contamination is amplified by poorly conditioned unregularized inversion, and optimal regularization suppresses the instability. The authors also connect this instability to runaway DEIM dynamics, where effective errors compound and regularization is estimated rather than demonstrated optimal.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes ROM sparse sensing and DEIM reconstruction error, rather than the original supervised-learning model-size, epoch, or training-sample sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The risk curves depend on sensor placement, projection onto leading modes, measurement noise or residual-mode contamination, pseudoinverse versus regularized reconstruction, regularization strength, and—in DEIM—the number of nonlinear modes q.

fits_no_version.finding: Time-integrated DEIM exhibits runaway trajectories near p ≈ q and reaches final-error plateaus with fewer sensors under regularized reconstruction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Static reconstruction instability can propagate into numerical instability of reduced-order dynamics.

record.problems: Evidence is specific to one SST dataset and one NSE example. NSE training and test sets are not separated because the snapshots are periodic. The authors report that some time-integrated values are missing where numerical integration diverges. Uncertainty is reported for empirical curves, but not for every result.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified results from the 16 SST design combinations or the additional plotted DEIM configurations were extracted beyond the outcomes described explicitly in the text.

untested.parts: No training-epoch sweep; PDE integration time is a different quantity.
No training-sample-size sweep. Additional sensors are measurements of a state, not additional training examples.
No capacity sweep into an overparameterized model regime. Reconstruction rank is fixed while additional sensors increasingly constrain the same latent coefficients.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, and samples. Matrix spectra predict instability in the particular reconstruction setup.
Label noise is not tested. Optimal regularization of time-integrated DEIM is not established; its regularization strength is estimated from residual-mode variance.
No effective-parameter recounting or transformation of double descent into a U-shaped curve.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Spike absence under optimal regularization or removal of noise is supporting evidence for V6, not a scope limitation. Additional plotted configurations are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model size is not varied.
Training epochs are not varied; time-integrated ROM error is not an epoch-wise training sweep.
Training sample size is not varied. The paper states that the number of snapshots is not used after the initial POD, but does not test increasing training data near a peak.
The study tests sparse-sensing and ROM risk against sensor count, not a broad range of model classes or conventional model-parameter capacity.
The study relates peaks to eigenvalues of a reconstruction matrix, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study tests measurement noise, subleading-mode contamination, and regularization in ROMs. It does not test label noise or explicitly test triple descent as such.
The study does not recount complexity by an effective number of parameters or test whether that transforms the curve into an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: Sea Surface Temperature dataset

conditions.value: projected onto the leading r modes

rows.value: When no pathological signal is present, p ≥ r reconstructs the signal perfectly (Rel.RMSE = 0).

rows.subject: Sea Surface Temperature dataset
rows.operation_detail: Swept the number of sensors p and measured reconstruction Rel.RMSE.
rows.value: The lowest eigenvalue quickly increases as sensors are added, the relative RMSE falls under 0.5, and the RMSE decreases slowly and monotonically across the sensor range.
rows.uncertainty: Empirical mean RMSE ± one standard deviation is shown.
rows.note: The regularized comparison has no low-lying eigenvalues and no double-descent spike.
rows.check: The monotonic regularized curve supports V6's suppression prediction; its version-relative state is observed. Remove V4.

rows.subject: Sea Surface Temperature dataset
rows.operation_detail: Swept regularization scaling Q and sensor count p; measured the resulting risk curves.

conditions.value: Q = 1 is the stated optimal strength; Q < 1 under-regularizes; Q > 1 over-regularizes

rows.value: Q = 1 is the lowest curve; Q < 1 produces a progressively steeper peak at p ≈ r; Q > 1 produces monotonic curves that gradually get higher.
rows.note: The result shows strong dependence of the spike on regularization strength.
rows.check: These are analytical DNA predictions, not separately measured empirical curves. Split under-, optimal-, and over-regularization into separate rows. Remove V4.

source_check.correct: Fig. 7 contains analytical DNA predictions, rather than separately measured empirical curves. rows.subject: Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (NSE) DEIM
rows.operation_detail: Swept sensor count p for static reconstruction of the nonlinear term.

conditions.value: noiseless and DNA-added noise of relative magnitude 10⁻³

rows.value: The regularized curve remains nearly flat at Rel.RMSE ≈ 100; pseudoinverse reconstruction is systematically worse, with a pronounced peak at p = q. For random sensors, noisy pseudoinverse error increases by orders of magnitude and is mostly above the plotted range.
rows.uncertainty: For random sensors at p = q, the error bar is the mean and standard deviation log-averaged over 50 random sensor-set replicas.
rows.note: The text reports these outcomes across the plotted q settings; it does not give separate numerical peak heights for each q.
rows.check: The nearly flat regularized error is approximately 10^0, or 1, rather than 100; superscript formatting was lost. Split reconstruction methods and noise conditions. Added-noise results are DNA predictions only. The 50-replica uncertainty applies to the p = q sweep in Fig. 9h, not all sensor-count curves. Remove V4.

source_check.correct: For random sensors, the nearly flat regularized curve has Rel.RMSE ≈ 10^0 = 1, rather than 100. Pseudoinverse reconstruction is worse and peaks at p = q. Added noise has relative magnitude 10^-3 and is evaluated only through DNA predictions. Separate reconstruction methods and noise conditions into individual rows.

rows.subject: Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (NSE) DEIM
rows.operation_detail: Swept sensor count p and measured final-time error after DEIM time integration.
rows.value: The error approaches an asymptotic form as p increases; runaway dynamics occur near p ≈ q, and some q = 3 and q = 6 values are missing at or near p = q because numerical integration diverges.
rows.note: The authors describe plateaus and divergence near the instability point, not a complete fall-rise-fall curve.
rows.check: This combines several ranks and both estimators. Final-time plateaus and numerical divergence do not establish a complete double-descent curve or test suppression under optimally tuned regularization.

source_check.notes: Several pack values are truncated; checks cover their visible assertions. The p = 35 eigenvalue band is not independently established as another error peak; DEIM regularization uses an estimated contamination strength.

statements.correction: POD-informed optimal regularization suppresses the SST instability; regularization is anisotropic (Sec. IV D). Under-regularization produces peaks, while optimal and over-regularization give monotonic curves (Fig. 7). Random placement produces an early spike at p = 24 (Sec. IV B). Removing both contamination and noise gives exact reconstruction for p ≥ r (Sec. II B).
statements.problem: The SST comparison involving a weak isotropic prior is not reported. This study uses a POD-informed anisotropic prior and varies its strength; R3 instead removes noise and residual-mode contamination.
